tips.comment: Market House won well by six and a half lengths at Fontwell last week and could follow up despite a seven pound penalty here at Stratford.

The model I run suggests Juan Bermudez can win this one. This result has been driven by Juan Bermudez having the highest RPR of the 7-runner field and is not overly penalized for it in the weights. Juan Bermudez goes out carrying only 2 lbs more than the current market favorite but according to RPR has potential for significantly more than that. Juan Bermudez came third when last out, which was the first run after a short break, and now has race fitness under his belt. Prior course and distance winner, so clearly likes this track and could go well again today. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Sir Galahad has won all three of his hurdle races despite being a maiden on the flat, he was however aided by his main rival falling late on last time. Could make it four from four as his handicap mark is not too testing and as a four year old he gets plenty of weight from Impero.
Alshadian comfortably won at Southwell a week ago in a two mile handicap chase and a seven pound penalty may not stop him folowing up at Stratford in a similar race.

The model I run suggests an upset can be caused here by Boom Boom. This result has been driven by Boom Boom having the highest RPR of the 7-runner field and the lowest official ranking. This subsequently leaves Boom Boom carrying the lowest amount of weight around this 2m trip. Has shown glimpses of return to form as well when running a decent third 30 days ago, so looks overpriced here. The model has issued a 'moderate' stake indicator, which translates to a 1pt bet on a scale of 0-4. This was driven by the small gap back to second in the race simulation but the large odds on offer relative to the win probability.

The model I run suggests Duel Au Soleil can win this one. Duel Au Soleil lines up here with the joint highest RPR of the smaller 6 horse race but goes out carrying 7 lbs less initial weight than the current top weight and market favourite Sergeant Fury. Duel Au Soleil has shown some decent form coming into this with a good second place finish only 17 days ago and now tries the tongue tie for the first time to go one better. Duel Au Soleil also has the highest top speed on the card by quite a bit, so if this is run at a slow pace, then turn of foot might be useful. The model has issued a 'high' stake indicator for this, which has mainly been driven by the size of the gap back to second in the race simulation and the value on offer at 4.33. This translates to a 4pt stake on a scale of 0-4.
Useful flat performer who has won 4 times and is making hurdling/stable debut. Holds every chance if taking to these obstacles

A Dublin Job has won his last three races and should make it four in a row from his new mark of 111 up 22 pounds for his three wins but only another four pounds for beating Davidoc three lengths on his first run for334 days.

the model I run suggests Davidoc can iwn this one. Davidoc lines up here with the second highest RPR of the 6 runner field but has the second lowest official ranking. That leaves him well treated off this mark and goes out carrying the second lowest amount of weight around this 2m 6f trip. Has been showing consistent improvement in his form figures, with results of 5432-2 , th latest 2n place finihs coming 27 days ago. Race fitness should not be a concern. model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Fame And Fun ( ex Paul Nicholls) acts on any ground and won a Chase very well in January 2m6f Fontwell, A lacklustre run over hurdles followed before another good chase effort over a trip on the sharp side for him at Ffos Las. Latest start he was highly tried in a class 2 and not much can be taken from that. Class 5 again today back up to 2m6f and at just 4lb higher than the emphatic win in January.

Going for a Dutch as 365 have got these prices wrong. This one ran a cracking second behind a progressive stable changer last time out, with the third winning in good style next time out. A similar performance and he has to be going close.

Really looking forward to seeing this horse over a sharp 2m as I do think his stamina was stretched over 2m2f at Downpatrick on his last outing over hurdles. The five-year-old arrives on the back of a triumph on the level and he definitely has the ability to be scoring in today's discipline.

the model I run suggests an upset from Postponed Legacy. This horse isn't too fancied in the early market, but Postponed legacy lins up here with a comaratively high RPR and an official ranking leaving him well treated off this market. As a result, goes out carriyng the second lowest weight around this 2m, 13 runner handicap hurdle. Has shown bits of fomr ocmimng into this too with figures of 535-34 all over this 2m handicap hurdle distance. Visors tried or the first time to eek out the bit that's missing to get over the line first. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicaotr whihc translates to a 0.5pt bet ona scal3 of 0-4.

Walk The Moon has had just 5 starts over hurdles and was 15l in front of Finn Russell at Wetherby in 2023 where he showed a real aptitude for this game. All hurdle starts since then ( bar one) have either been in better class or on softer ground. Has looked in good heart on recent flat runs and last hurdle start was here Oct 24 when he tried to make all but the softer ground found him out. He could bounce of the ground today and does get the trip so holds good EW appeal at the 20/1 available.
Favourite unlikely to be suited by this drop back to the minimum trip, whereas those that fought it out with Beerwah subsequently have gone close in decent races. Get's my vote here

Ruth Carr's form of late is very impressive, so maybe INVINCIBLE CROWN can outrun this price and get back to something like the run he demonstrated at Doncaster on handicap debut in April. That was a sixth place finish but he was only a couple of lengths away. Mark reduced now and the jockey booking looks a plus also. Hold-up run style is a negative but not enough to dissaude.

Go On Rosie might be worth another chance. Wasn't at best form last time out over 6f where she looked in need of the run, that was only her first run back from a rest so she could be arriving in better shape fitness wise with that last run out of the way. Drops back to 5f today which is the distance she's shown her best form, her best form has been shown on Good to Firm , should get those sort of conditions today. Today she runs from a 1 lb lower mark than last time and factor in the 5 lb claim by the jockey, she's looking well treated. Small each-way tip for today's NAP selection.
Is well bred being a half sister to a couple of winners in France. Likely to go well on debut and should be there or thereabouts
Did show some hints of promise on debut despite only finishing 6th of 8 on debut. Improvement likely and should be better than first race showed. Holds an each way chance

Blue RC won on debut and was unlucky not to make it 2 wins from 3 when beaten half a length at Kempton last time out. Makes handicap debut with the form boosted by last run (3rd that day has won since). Gets every chance off this opening mark

Daring Legend went close in a very warm race at York last time and if recreating that effort, surely has to go close here at a course (where like York, you need to get this distance well). Has to be the pick here.

Tried to make all over Donnys mile last time. Drops back to 7f which will suit and drops another oound. Hasnt won for a while but came close a couple of times last year from marks in the 80s. Big ew chance here
I think she is better suited to rurf so will welcome return back to turf tomorrow and dropped mark might present an opportunity to cause an upset win if fully focused.

Had a bad start on debut, led to being pushed early to keep up with the pace. Stayed nicely that day although running very green. Last time out, started better and ran midfield, hung badly near the run in, no match for winner but clear of 3rd. In with a great chance here (2pt win), jockey underrated in my opinion.

Golden Rainbow won over course and distance on last visit here and Kaiya Fraser who's in fine form with 22% win strike rate partnered up last time Golden Rainbow won a race - at Newcastle AW. Beaten less than a length on last 2 runs and forecasted good to firm conditions should suit. NAP
Had to come wide last time at Catterick but then rapidly got up some steam and went down by less than a length in the end. Back to win here.

Equity Law last won in April 2024 in a 0-100 graded handicap Off a rating of 83. He has been contesting higher grade races to what his current rating of 75 actually is. Todays opposition are running in or above their grades.
This is good placing by Tim Easterby and the horse under David Allan in taken to win comfortably. Equity Law is our nap today

JoJo Rabbit was winning for the 7th time in his career when taking advantage of a fall to his lowest mark at Ripon last week. He is back up 5lbs but his still 3lbs lower than his previous winning mark so looks to have a good chance of following up

Winner at Wolverhampton in September. Remained in decent form throughout the winter and ran well on turf at Lingfield last month. Is lurking on his last winning mark so should run well this afternoon.

Backing Birkenhead, the 8??'year??'old Captain Gerrard gelding trained by Paul Midgley, in tomorrow’s 6 furlong handicap at Thirsk. Despite his seasoned status, he returns in fine fettle??'reaching the frame recently over this same C&D off a career??'low mark, and two starts ago striking gold at Catterick in April on good??'firm ground . His official rating has been nudged down to around 67, presenting a chance now that he’s running off more favourable terms.
Birkenhead thrives on quick ground and handles Thirsk’s sharp, fast 6??'furlong straight well, especially from a low draw which could help his hold??'up style. He’s ran respectably in class 5 handicaps all season and, fresh off a confidence??'boosting run, looks ready to deliver another solid effort. He's proven he can stay competitive at this grade, and his veteran savvy could see him hit peak stride in the final furlong.
Got the splits towards the end of the race at Ripon last time and wasn't unduly pushed by the jockey when staying on. Is of interest as a result and figures as the bet here.
Has won twice at course and distance, showing good level of form and trainer nd Jockey among the winners lately

I’m siding with Muscika, the veteran 11-year-old gelding trained by David O’Meara, in tomorrow’s Grass Is Always Greener Handicap over 6 furlongs. Despite his age, he arrives in solid form??'winning two of just three starts this spring, including a tidy victory at Redcar over 5f in mid-May, and backing it up with respectable efforts: fifth at Chelmsford, fourth at Haydock, and a ninth at York on May 31, all over 6f and even softer turf . His seasonal peak suggests he’s primed for another bold run.
Rated around 71 and equipped with a wealth of experience, Muscika still carries a potent turn of foot and handles all ground types, including the prevailing good-to-firm conditions expected at Thirsk. His tactical versatility??'able to either race forward or settle midfield??'makes him well suited to a race likely to unfold at a decent pace. The thorough grounding he’s had this spring has sharpened him up, and he looks ready to go close.

Dark Kestrel is on a pretty lengthy losing streak at present but comes here on a career-low mark of 62, effectively 57 with Alex Jary's 5lb claim. He ran a good third of eleven with him riding off a mark of 74 back in March and we could see improvement on this his second outing since wind surgery.
Field Of Gold seemed to be unlucky not to win the 2000 Guineas and proved that to be the case when he bolted up in the Irish equivalent. He should prove difficult to beat here.

Has some great races on his CV (Breeders cup juvenile, more recently the french 2000 guineas) could have even more to give at this distance and will push the favourite right to the line. Trainer has won this race 9 times. One to watch.
Missed the derby after a bullish approach by the trainer - if remaining in similiar fettle, he must have a great chance here despite the favourites credentials.
Unlucky when met trouble last time. Stayed well on his first go at one mile and would have a big say from his form last year. Course winner who could run a big race.

I actually opt for the favourite to win the race but expect officer to give a good run for money at huge odds was going right way before Newmarket when behind some of these but trainer pitches back against them so not totally off the board here
Serious step up in class tomorrow but can still build on LTO effort at Sandown back in April of this year and despite limited experience, I do think he is overpriced.

A cracking race to start the meeting and Rosallion looks to have a great chance in this competitive Group 1 Queen Anne Stakes. He is unbeaten in 2 runs at Ascot and usually travels very well in his races. With a clear run he can make use of his potent turn of foot to win this.
Lead Artist is one that I am torn with for the pick as there are a lot of runners with G1 wins under there belt but for me having Colin Keane in the saddle is what tips my vote

Distance winner who won the 2000G last year on good going and also had a win in a Group 1 at Goodwood on good to firm(ish). Was off for six months before running a maybe ring rusty 4th of 8 in a Group 1 on 17th May. Will strip fitter for that today on ground that suits.

Little saver on this one who sneaks into an ew bet. Won his first two outings this year in a Listed and Group 2 race on ground with a bit of give and followed them up with a good 2nd of 8 in a Group 1 last time out against some of todays rivals.

Diego Velazquez won his first two races as a two-year-old and then disappointed in his next four races, three at Group 1 and then over 12f at Group 2 level here at Ascot. He was then dropped in distance and class for his last two races in Ireland last season and won both impressively at Group 3 and Group 2 level. He comes to Royal Ascot without a prep run but could be up to competing at Group 1 level over a mile.

My replacement for the opener is Lake Forest, who I just felt was rather thrown in here at the deep end up to a mile for the first time, and a stiff mile at that. He was dead last entering the last half furlong last time over 7f having been dropped in, and eased home late he passed beaten horses and ate up the ground. Often seen fast finishing over shorter, I’d hope he can be ridden a touch more prominently here as I’d think there’s a fair chance he’ll stay based on that, and with one of the pace angles out it is a concern if he’s dropped too far off the pace. His victory over Lazzat does bring him into the mix class wise albeit with a bit to find on figures. He’s entitled to improve for the run, as are many of these, but at double figure odds he looks a fair price.

Carl Spackler has been doing great in the USA with three G1 win out of the last four runs with the latest in April winning by over 4L and comes into todays race running for a new yard which can often put a bit more sping in the step EW
Unsuited by the shape of the course last time but still ran a huge race. Has strong form over this course and distance and suited by fast ground. good each-way.
Impressive on return winning a listed race in France. only question mark about the fast ground but tickes all the boxes otherwise. Could outrun his odds.

Despite his best efforts being well off the standard here, CAIRO maybe capable of more after finishing 2nd to The Foxes at big odds in the Group 2 Huxley Stakes at Chester 5½ weeks ago. He has placed five times in eight runs (63%) over 1 mile, winning twice (25%) & has placed seven times in nine runs (78%) within this sphere (class 1), winning twice (22%). Lively outsider.

Given the fact that Gstaad has got a precocious pedigree (related to Vandeek) and the taking nature of his debut, switching off the rail late to pick up the well baced favourite for same connections. Great chance here for a top outfit.
Military Code won his first two runs including here last month in a C3 on GF at 5f and I would expect more now third up and going to 6f

Won his only outing so far winning easily by 5L in a class 2 at Yarmouth quickening clear inside the final furlong of 6f 3yds on good to firm (good in places). Change of jockey today but trip and conditions suit.

Oisin Murphy must have been impressed by the way American Gulf came away from his field first time out at Windsor on the 2nd of June, as it is his choice of rides here. Although he may not have beaten much in the way of quality opposition, he should be at least placed here.
Ran out a very easy winner of a Maisen over 6f at the Curragh on race debit backmin early May and ran well next time out when third in a Group 3 back there behind a useful type. Good chance on form.

Warsaw romped home in impressive fashion on debut at Navan over 5f distance at the beginning of the month and looks the one to beat here stepping up to 6f distance which shouldn't be an issue as looked stronger the further the race went on in that win.

A wild Coventry as ever, and I’ll take a small stab at Rock On Thunder here who beat two subsequent winners on debut. He travelled quite sweetly into his debut before being strong at the line, and he beat Egoli 6L there who has won subsequently. That horse beat Lyrical Song about 9L since who had previously finished a few lengths behind Farough, who was beaten 2-3L by Coppull who reppposes here at a fair price. Logi Bear was between them, and he’s run a decent race in the Woodcote since, which in a rather twisted and roundabout way points me to this horse being overpriced. Bred to be better, and a pricey purchase, he looks worth a play in what is ultimately a bit of a lottery.

UNDERWRITER has a significant jockey booking with Australia's James McDonald coming in for the ride. That clearly means owners Wathnan Racing mean business and a high draw on the straight course sprinting across previous years has been a good place to be. Decent value.

Connections do pretty well with their youngsters and i doubt there will be much difference with Power Blue here. Was bought off other owners after coming second to high class Albert Einstein, looks a great bet at the odds.

I was rather impressed with the way Bone Marra came from last to first on debut and although it was a mere class 5 race and he was very green until rounding the turn his burst of speed was something else. This extra furlong should suit. Chrisophe Soumillon has good stats here with three wins and four places from fourteen.

Son of Ubettabelieveit, who has won a pair of Chester novices this spring, impressing on both occasions. This is quite obviously a very different test, but the numbers were good, so it would be no surprise to see him run well at a price.

Ballistic Missile did a grand job to win a C2 on debut last month with most of today's runners stepping up from C3,4 and 5 and I would expect to see a big step forward today after that strong run in which makes me think tant today's 6f could suit EW 4P

Coppull, I don't think, should be this big a price after it won a maiden which has produced several winners since it last ran. Yes, it's not seemingly this class, but it could have improved itself for trainer C Cox. The stable is not pulling up trees at the moment, but this is where it counts. D Probert rides.

A bit of a flier in the Coventry, but Kolkata Knight couldn't have been more impressive on debut, winning by 5L. With the second scoring since, there's some substance to that run. I like a horse ridden prominently here in the 2yo races as it removes the uncertainty of coming through a big field of inexperienced juveniles. I think the fact he's on the opposite side of the draw to the market principals could also be a positive should a draw bias become clear (stall 6 and under have won 4 of the last 6 runnings). The trainer has previous in 2yo races here, having trained a Queen Mary winner, and I think KK looks overpriced in a race which has seen big-priced winners pop up.
Well-bred SHAATIR is given a whirl at this price. Hollie Doyle gave him a winning ride last time out and with the progress these Havana Grey colts can make, maybe he gets involved here.
Very consistent sort who just failed to win a listed race last time. well suited by this course on previous run and looks open to further improvement now stepping up in trip.

DO OR DO NOT & the re-opposing Tadej was nicely clear when the latter got the upper hand in a novice Stakes at York 2½ weeks ago. That performance was a significant improvement from his debut run at Newbury 2 weeks prior. He has placed once in two runs (50%) over 6 furlongs & has also placed once in two runs (50%) on good or similar going. Lively outsider.

Last year Rashabar took the win in this race at 80/1. In 2020 Nando Parrado won 150/1. Race that can have a surprising winner. I will play Tadej at huge odds. A winner of Novice at York last month. Has a room for improvements and can surprise here.
HAve to say this one looks to have been laid out for this with Oision Murphy taking the ride won this last year and a repeat might just be possible
Believing was close in three G1 at the end of last term and returned in Meydan for a big money G1 win and worth a shot that she can follow that up

NIGHT RAIDER a colt is still considered an elite level five furlong sprinter by trainer Karl Burke and he needs respecting given this is his chosen race . A strong travelling type often up on the sharp end early , so presumably Wathnan Racing's first string with James Doyle riding he appeals.

Regional is joint oldest in the field as a seven-year-old but lost out in a battle throughout with Asfoora last year in this race, with both hanging right in the latter stages away from the stands side. He also finished just behind Believing in Meydan over 6f in April. He has not won since 2023 but should go close again from another high draw like last year, with a lot of his main rivals drawn middle to low.
Improving 5yo mare who has won both starts this year in very impressive style winning a Group 3 in France and Group 2 at Haydock. Has plenty of speed and looks a big player today.

Starlust won at the Breeder's Cup last year and looked really good on that fast ground over there. With 4 places on offer, fast ground on the menu and the in form Rossa Ryan/Ralph Beckett combo, this looks a good each way bet.

What a story this would be if American Affair could win this Group 1 sprint. He is lightning fast, and gets his ideal ground (good to firm), and hopefully doesn't meet any bad luck in running. My initial thoughts on him winning a sprint at this level was that the Nunthorpe might be the most likely, but Jim Goldie knows what it takes to get Ascot winners, so I trust he knows best.

On official ratings West Acre is only 2 behind the top rated in the race but with weight for age and penalties carries 6lb and 3lb less than these opponents. Seemingly best at 5f and probably on this surface, West Acre has a decent chance of improving which doesn't neccesarily apply to most of his opponents today. Assuming the ratings gained in Dubai are truly reflective of his ability he must go here with a good chance of hitting the frame at least.

Won Listed over CD in October & then after a 210 day break won Group 3 Palace House Stakes at Newmarket on Guineas day . Only managed 6th of 11 in Temple Stakes 24 days ago but being a previous CD winner can go well again here off decent each way odds .

Very speedy sort who was 5th in the Gp 2 Norfolk last year at this meeting and enjoyed a fruitful 2 yo campaign winning 4 of his 7 races including at Gp 3 & Gp 2 level. Not disgraced at the Breeders Cup on final start and is too big a price here. James Doyle rides Night Raider which is a slight worry but at the prices given this one didn't flop at this meeting last year as Night Raider did, in the Jersey he must be backed. Was a well backed favourite with Willie Buick booked on seasonal debut but ran as if needed the race and was too keen early on so should strip fitter here today and run a big race. Yet to convince at the highest level but hasn't had many chances but a stiff 5f in decent ground looks perfect and I'm expecting a big run.

David Egan is one of my main reasons for this selection, Adrian Murray has had a fine season so far, but the jockey booking is what makes the selection extremely valuable. Excels in positioning for this kind of race.

In great form on the turf with 5 wins and 5 places from just the 12 starts . Up to a Group 1 class today but has shown promise in listed company with a win and second from only the 2 starts that class . Worth a spec each way.

Big step up in class here after winning a Listed contest at York in mid May - travelled well and kept on in the final furlong as was always going to win. Broke a bit slowly which is a concern but could be running on at the end to grab a place.

Finished 5th in this race last year and ran well in competitive sprints for most of last season, Well beaten over 6f at York last month on seasonal return but should prefer this drop back down to 5f and has an each way chance.

Another one of my tracker horses who I noted as a 2yo. Only had one race as a 3yo almost a year ago and returned to action last month with a very ring-rusty 2nd at Haydock. Was held up in that race and had to wait for an opening, but was a little all over the place, which was probably the jockey's fault, but you can't be too harsh with such a lack of racing. My notes said back in Sept 23 that this was a 7f-8f horse and even that last race was over 6f, so it's a risky one now back to 5f, but I'll take the risk.

Manaccan looks and probably will be outclassed here, but its track record tells you it could sneak something 2/3! J Ryan, the trainer, has given this a shot with the very underrated C Fallon at massive odds.

I’m going to throw in one at a big price who looks a bit underestimated by the bookmakers and could easily outrun her 50/1 odds. No Half Measures may ideally prefer slower ground than she’ll get here, but she was a very progressive filly last year, winning both a Listed race and a Group 3 at Deauville and Newbury respectively, before running an excellent fifth in the Group 1 Prix de l’Abbaye on Arc day, where she didn’t get the clearest of runs. She improved plenty from her seasonal reappearance to go close at Haydock last time out. She’s shown her best form at tracks with stiff finishes, so I can definitely see her finishing off strongly. The draw isn’t bad either, so if she handles the slightly quicker ground, she could be one for the frame at massive odds.

A cracking King George III Group 1 stakes with my vote going to Twilight Calls a promising sprinter who was last seen at Haydock racing in the Betfred Temple Group 2 Stakes where finishing 9th/11 however that was just his second outing after a 237 day break having also exchanged ownership and yards in the process of that break and he is likely to be much better adjusted back home and in a much fitter state with 2 runs under his belt now this may be a competitive race but a good long analysis of this race clearly shows Twilight Calls will be well suited in a race of this nature R Spencer's new recruit looks poised for a big run here and ticks all boxes to do so and worth noting he ran very well in this race last year jockey J P Spencer takes the ride and can give Twilight Calls one of is master piece rides here at Ascot price atcthe time of writing represents very good E/W value with some firms offering more than 3 places in this if you shop around must be taken seriously and accordingly

I'm backing Frost At Dawn in tomorrow’s 15:40 King Charles III Stakes at Ascot. This lightly raced 4-year-old filly from William Knight's yard has been progressive this season, most recently landing the Listed Cecil Frail Stakes over 6f at Haydock on May 23 under Oisin Murphy . But the standout form reference is her eye-catching 33/1 upset win in Meydan’s Nad Al Sheba Turf Sprint (5f) under Mickael Barzalona??'where she led from the front and defied big odds on only her second ride for him .
Tomorrow she'll face a stronger field, but that same heart, speed, and versatility mark her out as dangerous. Ascot’s stiff 5f-plus layout will test her stamina over the final furlong??'something she’s demonstrated before when upped to 6f??'and with that Group??'winning turn of foot and experience proven on both turf and AW, she’s more than capable of featuring. The presence of proven Group 1 speedsters will ensure a strong gallop upfront, which should set her up perfectly to replicate her bold front-running tactics.

It's boring but I do think this is finally the year Willie Mullins lands this race. He sends a strong hand over and REACHING HIGH, whose dam is an Ascot Gold Cup winner, will take some beating if the breeding has gone as it should.

The James Owen trained East India Dock went up 8lbs for landing the Chester Cup by a length off 89 over 2m3f 39 days ago, which doesn't help. However the 4yo Golden Horn dual performing gelding will love the ground, stays the trip and has won in this grade, big e/w chance in a competitive cl2 h/cap.

As I've mentioned this just looks to be a Mullins year in this race and PONIROS, comes in well treated, and wasn't fair away when last seen here in September. Runs from the same mark today, this trip shouldn't be a problem and is probably in the shape of his life

Manxman has made the frame in 75% of his flat engagements and with a single figure draw and profile that suggests he will be plodding on when all other have raised the white flag, I am keen on Manxman's chances in the Ascot Stakes. Sean Bowen knows the horse well and if the handicapper still doesn't have a grip following his last time out success, he will go close again.
ALPHONSE LE GRANDE can put in a good show here for a trainer with an exceptional record in the race. Jamie Spencer knows the time of day around Ascot and can guide the horse home in front.

Mr Hampstead was aimed high as a three-year-old, running in both the Derby and then 18 days later in the Group 2 Queen's Vase here, where he tried to make all but finished 10th of 11. This season, he has run in a couple of two-mile handicaps at Goodwood, comfortably winning first time out and then being caught near the line by Manxman in his latest. He has gone up a combined nine pounds for the two runs but could still be competitive if his stamina holds out over the extra four furlongs.

Stayed on powerfully in the Irish Cesarewitch, the only one to make significant headway from the back despite getting stopped in his run. Very fair mark on the back of that autumn run and he shaped like the longer trip is within his reach.

Has only had 3 runs this season 1st of those 2nd in Listed at Nottingham , was 3rd of 4 in Group 3 Sagaro Stakes & then when stepping up in trip 39 days ago was a slightly disappointing 10th of 15 in Chester Cup over today's trip but I'll give her another try after finishing 2nd in this race last year & is 2Lb lower today .

Won the 2 mile 5 furlong Queen Alexandra at Ascot in 2023 and finished 3rd in the same race last year. Won over 2 mile at the Curragh in November 2024. Didn't run any race at Chester in early May but was drawn badly and got stuck on the outside. Will have a great chance of finishing in the first five at big odds if running the usual Ascot run.
Been running well in Ireland over shorter trips, finished a good 4th over this trip last time out,from top in form stable can go well off this mark
with 5 places up for grabs ascending looks great value at 22/1.he has won his last 2 races well and this step up in trip looks a big plus.he looks very well treated off of a mark of 95

Dominating this field is possible but no easy feat for LIARI, appealing as a type who will have no issues tackling this much longer trip after making all on return at Newmarket 4 weeks ago. Jockey Kieran Shoemark has won once in one ride (100%) when aboard & Liari has also won once in one run (100%) for trainer Michael Bell. One to watch.

Finished a 3L 6th in this race back in 2023 and gets another crack at it after once again doing well to finish 2nd in the Chester Cup last month. Apprentice ridden in that Chester race and this time has the excellent Oisin Murphy riding.

Very difficult to be particularly definitive here, given the race distance and the inexperience of most of these at this trip. The fairly unexposed, Jessie Harrington trained, Saturn looks like a thorough stayer in the making, and hopefully can run into a place at a big price. His last run at Cork was over a mile and a half, and not surprisingly that proved too short for him.

Was gonna give Royal Ascot a miss with regards to blogging, but looking at fantastic cards for the first two days and like alot of horse racing lovers no doubt, it got the better of me. Saying that I think I'll target the races that offer good each way places with 5 or more and look for some real value. Artistic Star is that value, but comes with caution as is not guaranteed to stay this marathon flat trip, but when seen last month stepping up to 14f for the very first time, wasn't beaten far and stayed on, potentially suggesting he could be worth chancing in this wide open affair. Jack Dace is value for his 7lb claim which puts my selection on his lowest career mark. Prolific owner Jeff Smith is an in form owner with 3 winners and 3 2nds in the last 9 days and this well bred son of Galileo could upset the more fancied runners. Bear in mind this is a handicap and he was 7th of 14 in the 2023 Epaom Derby.

FEIGNING MADNESS makes handicap debut having run with credit three times in Group 3 company. Each time he was ridden by Hector Crouch who would have provided feedback and trainer Ralph Beckett would have had many options for middle-distance or staying handicaps ahead of this week. A chance is taken with extra places offered.

You’re guessing with regards to the ground with this French raider, although his dam has produced horses that have appreciated a sound surface and the fact he’s entered with ground the way it is would suggest connections think he’ll take to it. A sound stayer on heavy ground, he looks very well treated off this mark of 91. 2.5L 2nd recently to May It Be who ran well enough in a decent listed event since chasing home 100+ rated horses. He’s no spring chicken so is clearly up against it against some more unexposed horses, but that’s more than baked into his price to chance him for me in a wide open affair.
French Master stayed the 1 mile 6 furlongs. Should improve again here. Got blinkers on for the first time and has a good chance.

Mullins and Moore have won the past two runnings of this race and there is no reason to suspect that the combo can't do it here again...this gelding certainly prefers flat racing to obstacles and will have a great chance.
CABALLO DE MAR could land this for a yard that usually does pretty well with its stayers. Still looks to have more in the locker and with Callum Shepherd retaining the ride surely he goes close.

AERONAUTIC looks the best bet on the card on day 1 of Royal Ascot. Travelling over from Ireland for this, the Joseph O'Brien trained 4yo is having only his second run a handicap here, having finished down the field in a pipe opener at the Curragh. This race looks like the target, stepping up in trip for this, I except to see far more accurately what this horse is capable of here.

Others probably hold slightly stronger winning claims but he has been producing a very solid run of placed form over about this trip for the last year. Oisin Murphy is a very interesting booking for a canny Irish trainer.

My second fancy on day one is the Irish raider from the Noel Meade yard and is the oldest in the field as a 9yo. Mixes flat racing with hurdling/chasing and was seen 22 days ago winning a Ballinrobe hurdle by an easy 12 lengths. He stays well and is another that can go well at a price.
Has some good form last year on the flat, has also been running well over the jumps before disappointing at Aintree. Claimer taking five pounds off will help alot as could be well handicapped

Progressive 4yo, winning 3 of his last 5 starts, all on the AW. Maybe going too quick at the front end last time out in Group 3. Comes here fresh after a 4-month break with likely improvement possible and kept fresh for this Ascot run. His turf mark is 10lb lower than his current AW mark, but he is proven on quick turf ground, only beaten a neck on fast turf ground last August in a useful £39K handicap. This race looks like a long-term target, and he has a strong jockey booking.

Has caught the eye as a hurdler in recent months, but before that ran well for Andrew Balding at this type of level. The NH type training may have given him stronger stamina to see this out, or it may have dampened his speed, the risk and opporunity of that dilemma is palatable at these prices.

Samui has disappointed several times since running 2nd in the Sky Bet Stayers Handicap over two miles at York last August off topweight on a mark of 102. He is back to that mark for this race over fourteen furlongs and has a decent draw in stall 5 for a position close to the rail throughout and Gordon Elliott has booked Colin Keane to ride.

Real Dream returned from a 210 day break in March to a decent C2 third but could not follow up in listed company last time out but I think the return to C2 today 1 lb lighter and having had that last run could be worth a shot with 5P on offer EW
Loughville bowled along latest at Goodwood probably no liking the track and will be more suited here under Rossa Ryan...Alan King trains

CRYPTO FORCE has twice previously been a Royal Ascot runner and festival repeaters can often perform well. Aimed higher previously this five year old could now be a horse at the peak of his ability and his two prep-runs so far this season have likely intentionally been over inadequate trips to protect his mark.
Never really got involved on seasonal return at Sandown lto but sure to come on for that run andthe stable does wel with runners in this hard to oppose
moved to a trainer who knows how to perforam at the big festivals and the booking of Ryan Moore more than catches the eye
Disapointed on return but didnt look genuine with the blinkers. Forget this run and from his form over this course last year, he would rate a big challenger.

James Doyle got HAATEM home at the festival last year and he's taken to repeat the feat with one that arrives in good shape with a couple of runs now under his belt this season. Enjoys the big occasion and looks a good each-way play.
Was a progressive three year old that landed a big race at Epsom after eight months off could improve on that display to go close here at a big price

Tricky race, with almost all of this having some sort of chance. I’ll be intrigued to see how Ecureuil Secret goes having done us a turn at Epsom, but this a quick turnaround and this is some set up so I can pass him over at the odds. At a similar price you have Torito who hasn’t been seen since placing in this last year, and he’ll do for me in first time cheekpieces. In the frame on each of his 7 starts, he’s got a solid record fresh and should come here a bigger stronger horse on ground that will not inconvenience. He rather sat in the stalls from an inside draw when 3rd in this last year, so assuming he doesn’t repeat that he could find a good spot from a slightly wider draw here. Whilst he’s rated towards the bottom of these he’s still not reached his ceiling, and if he’s ready he can hit the frame.
Meydaan won as a 2 year old in a listed race at Goodwood. Disappointing after that but improved after gelded won almost winning at Goodwood last time, has been well backed

Haunted Dream finished 2nd in this race last year and is better drawn this time in stall 4. He has not had a run since running 4th in a Group 2 in February at Riyadh but if fit and ready for his return he should go close again.

Liberty Lane did well last month with a third in a G2 and the beating Meydaan to win in listed company last time out and although taking on some weight for that he could still swing this and worth an EW 4P cance at the current price
Coming here in good form (411) but can be guilty of inconsistency but does have serious ability and does look a bit over priced to me especially helped by a drop down in class.

I cannot get my head around AMBIENTE FRIENDLY being 16/1 here (4 places). Yes the 2024 Derby runner-up has failed to live up to expectations, but this is a drop into listed company after going off joint favourite on his last two starts at Gr3 and Gr2 respectively. The jockey has failed to settle him on both starts this term after a switch to the J Owen yard in the winter so I’m hoping that connections have finally unpicked his headstrong nature and the big field will mean that he can get plenty of cover. R Havlin renews acquaintances which is a positive given 2 of his 3 rides on him has proven fruitful including that Epsom Derby and 1.25l 3rd in the Irish Derby. Owen is a master at giving horses a small break of 29 to 56 days (23% SR, A/E 1.73) and his 24% SR (A/E 1.48) on good ground is another string to their bow.
This horse won a Group 3 two starts ago, beating a horse who went on to win a Group 1 afterwards. It carries a penalty for the Group 3 win, but may be up to the task dropped in grade.

DOHA was aimed at this meeting last year with the same single prep-run behind her. She was successful last June in an all fillies handicap fending off potential big improvers that day and trainer Ralph Beckett understands better than most where to aim this type. Looking capable in Listed company she makes each-way appeal.

Despite a few of these looking stronger, CHECKANDCHALLENGE has looked as good as ever this term including when 5th to Lead Artist in the Group 1 Lockinge Stakes at Newbury 4½ weeks ago. He has won once in nine runs (11%) over 1 mile 2 furlongs & has placed ten times in twenty-seven runs (37%) for trainer William Knight, winning four (15%). Lively outsider.

PHANTOM FLIGHT may be able to pull out a bit more to take this, after plugging on for 3rd in the Group 3 Brigadier Gerard Stakes at Sandown 3 weeks ago. Jockey Callum Shepherd has placed five times in ten rides (50%) when aboard, winning three (30%) & Phantom Flight has placed ten times in nineteen runs (53%) on good or similar going, winning six (32%). Lively outsider.
Another cd horse for course is S Bin Suroor runner Passion and Glory which is 2/2 here and looks forgotten.nice to see the very able Rossa Ryan up ew

Thius C Hills trained 3-y-o filly has finished second in her first two races over six furlongs and seven furlongsthe latest over seven furlongs at Kempton coming back from a 205 day breakto be beaten 1 1/2 lengths behind the J Butler trained Emery Down so back down in trip with Jason Watson onboard she can make it third time lucky today

Spirit Of Jenny made a good impression on her Leicester debut, looking to get the hang of things quickly, making headway and keeping on. Trainer Steph Hollinshead stated, in the winners enclosure, that she had given this big filly plenty of time but liked her a lot. There may be improvement to come.
Lokma comes here after winning a class 3 novice race open to improve a lot I would imagine Trevor Whelan takes the reigns and in a very winnable handicap race

Winner of his new yard debut at Wolverhampton on the 5th of April 2025 and was last seen at Nottingham 16 days ago where finishing a respectable 4th/8 and he did shape better than that bare result suggests currently operating on a mark of 73 R M Beckett's inmate is surely capable of better in my point view as this is a suitable looking assignment that shouldn't take much winning for a horse of this level as this race is not as competitive as it may seem at a quick glance jockey R Kingsgote takes the ride on this on this daughter of Zoustar & Moretta Blanche ( Dam's sire Dansili ) and can give her the perfect ride here at Southwell merits consideration

Victors Dream 5 year old bay gelding. Not the best horse in the world but he did perform well at Brighton 2 runs ago, disappointed on next start but has a stronger jockey on today and should perform better here.

Sir Benedict's form figures for Southwell read 2731127, the second place was here on May 1st and he has since ran a poor seventh of nine over six furlongs on turf at Doncaster. He drops back to five furlong today and should make the frame.

The Darryll Holland trained Kameko Spirit as a 3yo gets in this cl6 Classified Stakes off a joint bottom weight of 9-2. The Kameko filly is a 7 race maiden on the AW but has gone close on a couple of occasions and looks a solid e/w play in this company.
Only finished 9 of 11 at Leicester LTO earlier this month but will wlecome return back to AW as he poses much more of a threat on this surface and hoping first-time visor does the trick.
Time allowed is being stepped up in trip with a stable who does very well with this tactic I think time allowed is the one to beat here. Short and sweet
Taking a big leap of faith here, but the Bethell yard hasn't been too bad with newcomers and is related to decent horses over this distance (Imperial Fighter jumps to mind). Great chance to place
Returned from a 10 month break to finish 3rd on stable debut at Wolverhampton earlier this month. Each way chance again if finding some improvement
Hibernate is gradually being upped in trip by new connections and i think that the pedigree suggests that this horse will continue to be suited by increases in trip
All 3 career wins have been on the all weather at Newcastle but has been running consistently well of late with 4 placings from last 5 starts. Should be there or thereabouts

Daughter of Showcasing & Music Show ( Dam's sire Noverre ) who was last seen at Beverley 42 days ago where finishing 6th/7 however he most certainly needed the run after a 119 day break and he has now dropped to an attractive mark of 66 racing in a very suitable looking race here and is more than capable of bouncing back to his best here jockey Ray Dawson takes the ride on M Appleby's inmate and can give Noisy Music a promising ride here at Southwell must be taken very seriously

I’m reluctantly siding with Spartan Fighter, the veteran 8-year-old Dutch Art gelding trained by Antony Brittain, in the Highbet Club Acca Boost “Confined” Handicap (7 f 14 y) at Southwell. While his recent turf form isn’t compelling??'finishing outside the top four at Redcar (10th, May 26) and Newcastle (fifth, May 2)??'his proven ability to fire over this all-weather course keeps him in the mix . His last AW win came at Newcastle in February and his most recent Was??'Favored success was at Southwell in March, showing he still handles the surface well .
Off a reduced mark (OR mid-50s) and dropping into a confined Class 5 field, he could squeeze into a place with a patient ride. Expect him to break handy and settle into a stalking position before aiming to pick them off late, as he did in March’s Newcastle victory. His best chance rests on getting back on the Southwell tapeta where he’s comfortable.

Beaten favorite last time , still a bit green but will come on with a longer distance , trainor in good form 
will be there at the finish .
First time visor did the trick last time when winning for the first time at the 17th attempt. Carries a penalty but every chance of following up if in the same form

Sam James gave quite a positive vibe about the chances of Reverberate when asked at Carlisle on Monday. He is obviously going to stay well as the yard have waited for seven furlong races to commence. He's in the right hands, and, although a short price, looks a sound bet.
lots to like about Kalaganov in this race has several good place efforts over the distance this term must go close in this event today

Had a day to forget LTO when 10 of 11 at Newcastle last September but it helps he does have experience winning over C&D but doe shave a chance if he can overcome rustiness as it will be first run in about 8 months.
She is not coming here in the best of form but it helps she's a C&D winner and just 3lbs higher than last winning mark, given use of a 3lb claimer. Also helps driopping down in class.

Lincoln Rockstar won five times last year, three of them over this course and distance. Clearly likes this track and showed a return to form at Leicester last time out so repeat of that effort should see him competitive here.

Ancient Myth 4 year old bay gelding. Harshly given an initial handicap mark of 80 and after2 poor runs it went down to 73 and he performed much better on that mark finishing 3rd at Ripon. Same mark here looks value at around 11/2.
Original outlaw brings solid potential form suggests he should remain competitive and may benefit from stalking and finding cover early on and finishing the race strongly.

Was totally unfancied by the markets when making his racecourse debut in a maiden at Haydock over an extended 8f. There were clear signs of inexperience in the early stages of that race but shaped with promise late on without coming under too much pressure. Better can be expected and can reward each way support.
Devasboy has been somewhat frustrating since being noted when a good second at Wolverhampton nine runs ago. Ran a good third off 2lb higher three runs ago and is on a handy mark at present.
Panama City is quite consistent for a horse that runs at this lowly grade. He likes the track, ran well here last time, and enjoys the services of the talented apprentice Shay Farner.

A previous winner over the extended 7 furlongs here but is a winner over a furlong further on tapeta twice, most recently when last seen on the 27th of May. The drop in trip with a fast pace will suit.
